findings.claim: The change edits `MessagePackSecurity.DepthStep` from `>=` to `>`. Nothing in REQ-2234 asks for this, and it is a security behaviour change. A graph nested exactly `MaximumObjectGraphDepth` levels deep used to throw `InsufficientExecutionStackException` and is now accepted, so the depth limit (500 by default) effectively becomes limit+1 for all users. The requirement is limited to the analyzer and `SuppressSourceGeneration`, and ledger L12 covers a different depth change.

receipt_plan.detail: Build a msgpack payload of nested arrays exactly `MessagePackSecurity.Default.MaximumObjectGraphDepth` levels deep. Deserialize it as `object` with `MessagePackSerializerOptions.Standard`. Base throws `MessagePackSerializationException` (inner `InsufficientExecutionStackException`); head succeeds.

findings.claim: No changed line references `SuppressSourceGeneration`. The only analyzer-side changes stop a crash on duplicate or mixed keys: `Dictionary.Add` throwing turns into AD0001, which kills the analyzer. If base instead skips `SuppressSourceGeneration` types entirely, ordinary diagnostics are still missing. For example, MsgPack004 for a public member without `[Key]` would not be reported, so the core acceptance criterion would be unmet. The new README text would then also claim validation that does not happen.

receipt_plan.detail: Run `Receipts.GeneratedTests.SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.SuppressedType_MissingKey_ReportsMsgPack004` on head. It must pass, i.e. MsgPack004 is reported for `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` with an un-keyed public property.
